title: The multiples of 10
keyIdea: Ten ones can be tied into one bundle called a ten. The multiples of 10 are 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80 and 90: they are one to nine tens and 0 ones. In 60 the 6 counts tens and the 0 says there are no loose ones. The 0 keeps the 6 in the tens place, so 6 tens is written 60, not 6. Number words that end in -ty name tens: sixty is 6 tens. Counting in tens adds one ten each time, so only the tens digit goes up.
familyTip: Tie dry pasta, straws or lolly sticks into bundles of 10 with a hair band. Grab a few bundles and ask: how many tens, and what number is that? Then say it the other way: show me 70. Listen for sixty and sixteen and ask which one has more tens.

visual.caption: Is it a -ty number or a -teen number? Drag each card into a box, or tap it and then a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: tie sticks into tens, make 60 on a mat, write 40 and 70, match sixty and sixteen, and jump to 100 in tens.

kid: Count 10 sticks. Put a band round them. Now it is one bundle. We call it a ten. It is still 10 sticks. Count the bundles. 3 bundles is 3 tens. That is 30. 6 bundles is 6 tens. That is 60. There are no loose sticks, so there are 0 ones.
Look at 60. The 6 is in the tens place. The 0 is in the ones place. The 0 says no loose ones. If you leave off the 0, you write 6. That is only 6 sticks!
Listen to the words. Sixty ends in -ty. It means 6 tens. Sixteen ends in -teen. It is 1 ten and 6 ones. Sixty is much bigger.
Count in tens: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90. Each jump adds one bundle. Only the first digit goes up. After 90 comes 100. That is 10 tens.
adult: Ages 6 to 7. Common Core 1.NBT.B.2 says children should understand that 10 can be thought of as a bundle of ten ones, called a ten, and that 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80 and 90 refer to one to nine tens and 0 ones. In England, Year 1 counts in multiples of ten and Year 2 recognises the place value of each digit in a two-digit number. Key words: ten, ones, bundle, multiple of 10, tens digit, ones digit, place value, zero holding the ones place.

The idea moves a child from counting single objects to counting groups as units. A ten is one thing worth ten, so 6 tens can be counted on six fingers but is worth 60. The zero is not decoration: it holds the ones place so the 6 stays in the tens place. This is the base for counting in tens from any number, adding and subtracting multiples of 10, and for 100 as ten tens.

Common mistakes: counting the sticks and calling 50 '50 tens'; writing 6 tens as 6 because the zero 'is nothing'; confusing sixty with sixteen, since English -ty and -teen sound alike; counting on by ones (20, 21) when asked to count in tens; and thinking the 0 in 90 means there is nothing at all. Watch also for children who say 'ten-ty' or write 100 as 1000 after 90.

In the lab children tie 30 loose sticks into three bundles, lay six bundles on a mat to make 60 (a single stick is refused because 60 has no ones), and write 40 and 70 with digit tiles in a Tens box and a Ones box. They then match sixty, sixteen, forty and fourteen to bundle pictures and jump a frog from 0 to 100 in tens.

practice.prompt: The multiples of 10: what number is 6 tens and 0 ones?
practice.hint: Each ten is a bundle of 10 sticks. Count in tens six times.
practice.explain: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60. Six tens is 60. 6 would be 6 loose ones, and 16 is 1 ten and 6 ones.

practice.prompt: You have {t} bundles of 10 sticks. How many sticks is that?
practice.hint: Count in tens, one ten for each bundle: 10, 20, 30 and on.
practice.explain: {t} bundles of 10 is {t} tens, and {t} tens is {=10*t}. There are no loose sticks, so the ones digit is 0.

practice.hint: Look at the tens digit. The 0 in the ones place means no loose ones.
practice.explain: {=10*t} is {t} tens and 0 ones, so there are {t} tens. Each ten is 10 sticks.

practice.hint: Words that end in -ty mean tens. Forty means 4 tens.
practice.explain: Forty is 4 tens and 0 ones: 40. Fourteen is 1 ten and 4 ones: 14. 4 is just 4 ones.

practice.prompt: Count in tens: {=10*t}, {=10*t+10}, ... What comes next?
practice.hint: Each jump adds 1 ten. The tens digit goes up by 1 and the ones digit stays 0.
practice.explain: {=10*t+10} is {=t+1} tens. One more ten makes {=t+2} tens, which is {=10*t+20}.

pool.hint: Count the bundles, not the sticks. 50 is 10, 20, 30, 40, 50.
pool.explain: 50 is 5 tens and 0 ones. 50 is the number of sticks, not the number of bundles.

pool.prompt: Mia has 7 bundles of 10 straws. How many straws is that?
pool.hint: Each bundle is 1 ten. 7 bundles is 7 tens.
pool.explain: 7 tens and 0 ones is 70. 17 is 1 ten and 7 ones, and 7 is only 7 straws.

pool.prompt: In 90, what does the 0 tell you?
pool.hint: The 0 is in the ones place. What does the ones place count?
pool.explain: The 9 shows 9 tens. The 0 is in the ones place and says there are no loose ones. It keeps the 9 in the tens place.

pool.prompt: Count in tens: 30, 40, 50. What comes next?
pool.hint: Add one more ten. Only the tens digit goes up.
pool.explain: 50 is 5 tens. One more ten is 6 tens: 60. 51 is 1 more, and 70 skips a ten.

pool.prompt: Write {t} tens and 0 ones as a number.
pool.hint: Put {t} in the tens place and 0 in the ones place.
pool.explain: {t} tens and 0 ones is written {=10*t}. The 0 keeps the {t} in the tens place.

pool.hint: Sixty ends in -ty, so it means tens: 6 tens.
pool.explain: Sixty is 6 tens: 60. Sixteen ends in -teen and is 1 ten and 6 ones: 16.

pool.prompt: Sam writes 8 tens as 8. What did Sam forget?
pool.hint: Where does the 8 sit if it is on its own?
pool.explain: On its own, 8 sits in the ones place and means 8 ones. Writing 80 puts the 8 in the tens place, with 0 ones.

pool.prompt: Count back in tens from {=10*t}. What comes next?
pool.hint: Counting back takes away 1 ten. The tens digit goes down by 1.
pool.explain: {=10*t} is {t} tens. One ten fewer is {=t-1} tens, which is {=10*t-10}.

pool.prompt: Which is more: 3 tens or 9 ones?
pool.hint: Turn the tens into a number. 3 tens is 30.
pool.explain: 3 tens is 30 and 9 ones is 9, so 3 tens is more. A bundle is one thing but it is worth 10.
